history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE ALERT: this row (seq 2037) is the SAME gurdwara already recorded as seq 812 ('Gurdwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib', Ludhiana) - same name, same town, same Field Ganj location. It is not a separate site. THIS IS A SIKH GURDWARA, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE. Gurdwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib ('the eradicator of suffering') stands in the Field Ganj area of Ludhiana, opposite the Jagraon Bridge, in the heart of the city. It is one of Ludhiana's best-known gurdwaras: travel guides report about 50,000 devotees of different religions visiting daily, and it claims to be the first gurdwara in India to project Gurbani hymns on wide screens during kirtan so the congregation can follow along. The official website is gdnsldh.org. IMPORTANT SOURCE CONFLATION FLAG (carried from seq 812): many web pages (e.g. 99mustsee, some YouTube descriptions) paste the history of Gurdwara Dukh Nivaran Sahib at PATIALA onto this Ludhiana gurdwara - the story of Bhag Ram of Lehal, Guru Tegh Bahadur's visit on 24 January 1672 (Magh Sudi 5, 1728 Bikram), Raja Amar Singh of Patiala's garden, Maharaja Bhupinder Singh and Maharaja Yadavindra Singh's 1942 building. That documented history belongs to the Patiala shrine (see Wikipedia's 'Gurdwara Dukh Nivaran Sahib', which locates it in Patiala), not the Ludhiana one. One travel page instead claims the Ludhiana gurdwara is linked to Guru Hargobind in the '18th century' - itself inconsistent (Guru Hargobind lived in the 17th century). The Ludhiana gurdwara's own founding story is therefore UNVERIFIED; do not repeat the Patiala account as this gurdwara's history. Note also: a similarly named Gurudwara Sri Dukh Niwaran Sahib at 22 Feet Road, Haibowal Kalan, is a different Ludhiana gurdwara (verify).

name: Gurudwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib
town_description: Ludhiana is Punjab's largest industrial city, set on the Grand Trunk Road along the old course of the Sutlej. It is predominantly Sikh, with several major gurdwaras; Gurdwara Dukh Niwaran Sahib stands in the busy Field Ganj locality opposite the Jagraon Bridge, close to the railway station.

travel.airport: Sahnewal Airport (Ludhiana) has limited service (verify); nearest major airport is Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~135 km) or Chandigarh (~100 km).
travel.railway: Ludhiana Junction (major station on the Delhi-Amritsar line) is about 2 km away (verify); autos and cycle rickshaws to Field Ganj.
travel.road: Field Ganj is central Ludhiana, on NH-44/GT Road corridor; easily reached by city buses, autos and taxis.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Gurpurabs for major congregations (crowded).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listings give roughly 3:00/4:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily (verify). Langar (free community meal) is served; cover your head and remove shoes before entering.
